# Osaka Notes

## Overview

Three nights in Osaka in April 2024, in a hotel two streets back from the Dotonbori canal. I came down on the local train, about forty minutes with one change, and spent the first evening simply walking the canal and watching the crowds. Osaka felt louder and friendlier than the cities earlier in the trip, and almost everything I wanted sat within a thirty-minute walk or a two-stop subway ride.

## Food

Dotonbori is the obvious starting point and it earns the crowds after dark. I ate takoyaki from a stall near the Ebisubashi bridge, eight pieces for 500 yen, hot enough to burn my mouth twice. The Kuromon market was better in the morning, before the tour groups arrived; I bought a tuna skewer and a strawberry mochi and sat on a low wall to eat. Okonomiyaki was the other highlight, cooked on the table at a small place in Shinsekai, and I ended most evenings with a bowl of udon near the hotel.

## Notes

Osaka castle park was quiet on a weekday morning and the moat walk took about an hour. The subway day pass paid for itself after three rides. I used cash at the market stalls and cards everywhere else. One rainy afternoon went to the Umeda department store food halls, a better use of the time than standing in the aquarium queue. The covered shopping arcades are the trick in wet weather, and they run for kilometres without a gap.
